opt:body.p: A frame-by-frame player for the interaction reports, built from the site's own vocabulary so the reports can render and exercise themselves. A centred stage shows the current frame; a still strip of every frame pages forward under a travelling marker; a chart of the sampled properties carries the playhead and the chapter bar. Hover the chart or the strip to peek without moving the playhead; press the chart to scrub; press a strip frame and drag to choose, release to seek, Escape to cancel. Keys while focused follow the familiar model: Space or K, comma and period to step frames, arrows, J and L, Shift with an arrow for one second, Page Up and Page Down by chapter (Ctrl or Alt with an arrow does the same), digits, Home and End, the angle brackets for speed.

Series take their colour from the palette tokens (--op-series-1 to 6, fitted per theme and tested for contrast and colour-vision separation), but colour is never the only cue: each series after the first has its own dash pattern, a labelled series ends in a direct label with a swatch, an unlabelled one carries markers, and under forced colours or a high-contrast preference every paint maps to a system colour with the dashes and markers keeping the series apart.

With a video attribute naming a recording of the same window, the stage plays it in place of the sheet's frames, on the film's own clock: play, pause, seek and rate all apply to the video, and the sheet stays underneath as the poster. The interaction reports record one from the browser's screencast for every film.

Every render broadcasts the clock, so other views of the same timeline stay on it. The event is opt-film-time, it bubbles and crosses shadow boundaries, and its detail is the object { time, duration, playing }: the current time and the timeline's length, both in seconds, and whether the film is running. An opt:machine with a for naming the film reads the time field to move its token.

opt:film.title: Eight frames of a theme flight
